findings.evidence: "A threshold is the numeric boundary that triggers an alert once a metric crosses it."
findings.fix: Remove this sentence or move it to a conceptual/reference document, leaving this section with only the two actions (open panel, select rule).
findings.location: "## Open alert settings" section, second sentence
findings.violation: This is a conceptual definition dropped into the middle of a procedural step list, breaking the action sequence of a how-to document that should contain only task-oriented instructions.

findings.evidence: "confirm the unit matches the metric in use"
findings.fix: State where the metric's unit is shown (e.g., next to the metric name in the rule editor) or list which units apply to which metrics.
findings.location: "## Set the new threshold" section, first sentence
findings.violation: The reader is told to "confirm" a match but is given no way to know what the correct unit is or where to check it, so the instruction can't actually be carried out.

findings.evidence: "This is because the console applies the new threshold to every future evaluation of this rule."
findings.fix: Replace with a reason that actually relates to unit matching (e.g., "a mismatched unit will cause the alert to fire at the wrong value"), or delete the sentence.
findings.location: "## Set the new threshold" section, second sentence
findings.violation: The "This is because" clause doesn't actually explain the preceding instruction about matching units - it describes something unrelated (that the setting persists for future evaluations), making the causal link a non-sequitur.

findings.evidence: "Save the rule and open the rule list to confirm the new threshold appears there."
findings.fix: Add a step to run a test evaluation or check the rule's recent evaluation/alert history to confirm the new threshold behaves as expected.
findings.violation: This only confirms the displayed value, not that the rule evaluates correctly at the new threshold, so a rule that is broken in some other way would still pass this "verify" step.

findings.evidence: absence of any mention of required access level before the steps begin
findings.fix: Add a short prerequisites line (e.g., "Requires Editor or Admin role") before "## Open alert settings".
findings.violation: The guide never states what permissions are needed to edit an alert rule, so a reader without edit rights could follow every step and only discover the blocker at "Save" with no explanation.
